new_cultures.name: Southeastern US
new_cultures.culture: African-influenced Southern cooking with rice cultivation, pork, and okra
new_cultures.diet_signature: The Southeastern US diet emerged from the fusion of African, Native American, and European culinary traditions. Characterized by rice cultivation from West African knowledge, heavy use of okra, black-eyed peas, and pork, with a preference for slow-cooked, richly flavored dishes. Cornbread, greens, and sweet potatoes are staples alongside various seafood from coastal areas.

new_cultures.name: California Coastal
new_cultures.culture: Acorn-based indigenous diet with salmon, shellfish, and seeds
new_cultures.diet_signature: California coastal indigenous peoples developed sophisticated food systems centered on acorn processing, salmon runs, and marine resources. Acorns were leached and ground into flour, complemented by abundant shellfish, salmon, seeds, and game. The diet was remarkably diverse with seasonal variation and included extensive use of native plant foods.

new_cultures.name: Siberian
new_cultures.culture: Extreme cold-adapted diet with reindeer, horse, and preserved foods
new_cultures.diet_signature: Siberian diets evolved for extreme cold survival, featuring preserved and fermented foods that could last through brutal winters. Reindeer provides meat, fat, and organs while horse meat is prized. Fish is frozen raw (stroganina) or fermented. The diet is very high in fat and protein with minimal carbohydrates, supplemented by wild berries in summer.

new_cultures.name: Sichuan/Southwest China
new_cultures.culture: Bold, numbing flavors with Sichuan peppercorn, chili, and preserved vegetables
new_cultures.diet_signature: Sichuan cuisine is defined by its bold, complex flavors featuring the distinctive numbing heat of Sichuan peppercorns combined with chili peppers. The humid climate led to extensive preservation techniques including pickling, fermenting, and drying. Rice is the staple grain with frequent use of pork, tofu, and seasonal vegetables in intensely flavored sauces.

new_cultures.name: Western Indian
new_cultures.culture: Vegetarian traditions with millet, lentils, and coastal coconut influences
new_cultures.diet_signature: Western Indian cuisine spans from the vegetarian Gujarati and Rajasthani traditions to coastal Goan and Maharashtrian influences. The diet emphasizes millet and lentil combinations, extensive use of yogurt and ghee, and distinctive sweet-savory flavor profiles. Coastal areas incorporate more seafood and coconut, while interior regions favor millet-based flatbreads and preserved foods.

new_cultures.name: Brazilian Coastal
new_cultures.culture: Afro-Brazilian fusion with dendê oil, cassava, and seafood
new_cultures.diet_signature: Brazilian coastal cuisine, especially from Bahia, represents a vibrant fusion of African, Indigenous, and Portuguese influences. Characterized by dendê (red palm oil), coconut milk, cassava/manioc, and abundant seafood. The African influence is strong in cooking techniques and ingredient combinations, creating distinctive dishes unlike other South American cuisines.

modern_substitutes.Dendê oil: Combination of palm oil and paprika for color

new_cultures.name: Gaucho (Pampas)
new_cultures.culture: Grassland pastoralist diet centered on grass-fed beef and yerba mate
new_cultures.diet_signature: The Gaucho diet of the South American pampas is one of the world's most meat-centric, built around grass-fed cattle raised on vast grasslands. Beef is consumed in large quantities with minimal processing, often simply salted and grilled. Yerba mate provides vitamins and caffeine. Vegetables are minimal, with the diet historically very high in protein and fat.

modern_substitutes.Organ meats: Grass-fed beef cuts for those unfamiliar

new_cultures.name: Canadian Prairies
new_cultures.culture: Plains and Subarctic fusion with bison, pemmican, and wild rice
new_cultures.diet_signature: The Canadian Prairies diet represents a fusion of Plains indigenous foodways and Subarctic influences. Bison was the primary protein source, preserved as pemmican for winter survival. Wild rice harvested from lakes, berries, and root vegetables supplemented the meat-heavy diet. The harsh climate required high-fat, nutrient-dense foods that could be stored long-term.

new_cultures.name: Australian Coastal
new_cultures.culture: Coastal Aboriginal diet with oysters, fish, and estuarine resources
new_cultures.diet_signature: Australian coastal Aboriginal peoples developed sophisticated marine harvesting practices over 65,000 years. Rock oysters, fish, shellfish, and estuarine resources formed the protein base, complemented by coastal plants, seeds, and seasonal inland game. The diet was sustainable, seasonal, and highly nutritious with excellent omega-3 fatty acid profiles from marine foods.

modern_substitutes.Kangaroo/Emu: Grass-fed beef or lamb (though kangaroo is commercially available)
